description: The second run ranges from Greek mythology and maritime mystery to aviation, mountaineering, northern European geography, Monopoly, vocabulary and surveying, with each subject offering a fresh way to turn recognition into uncertainty.

s02e01.description: Greek mythology opens the new year in suitably dramatic fashion with the queen of the underworld. Gods, legends and general knowledge share the ladder, producing the familiar Millionaire problem: knowing the story is easier than trusting the answer.

s02e02.description: The Mary Celeste brings one of history’s great maritime mysteries into the hot seat. The rest of the quiz moves through equally varied territory, though few subjects can compete with an apparently abandoned ship for instant episode identity.

s02e03.description: Three names form the episode’s most peculiar little constellation: Dallas, Brett and Kane. It is exactly the kind of question detail Millionaire excels at making suddenly important, surrounded by a ladder that refuses to stay in one intellectual postcode.

s02e04.description: Britain’s Three Peaks Challenge gives the episode some literal elevation. Geography and endurance make a memorable stop on a ladder that otherwise climbs by knowledge rather than altitude, with every new question offering its own small summit.

s02e05.description: Skagerrak and Kattegat turn northern European geography into something that sounds almost invented. The paired waterways make an ideal Millionaire curiosity: distinctive, slightly intimidating, and just familiar enough to make doubt especially irritating.

s02e06.description: The London Monopoly board transforms a familiar game into a test of suspiciously specific memory. Streets, colours and cultural knowledge mingle in an episode where knowing something casually is repeatedly shown to be inferior to knowing it precisely.

s02e07.description: A condor soars into the episode’s question set and gives it a clean, memorable identity. Natural history joins the usual mixture of culture and general knowledge, with the ladder proving that even familiar creatures can become awkward under studio lights.

s02e08.description: Aerodynamics contributes the delightfully technical Gurney flap, a tiny device with a disproportionately good name. It epitomises the episode’s appeal: ordinary confidence meets a term that specialists know instantly and everyone else suddenly wishes they did.

s02e09.description: History becomes considerably less dignified when a famous naked horseback ride enters the quiz. The episode moves between respectable knowledge and wonderfully strange detail, demonstrating that education is apparently best retained when clothing is optional.

s02e10.description: A deceptively ordinary word proves anything but quotidian as vocabulary becomes the episode’s defining curiosity. Language, culture and general knowledge mingle while a perfectly usable English word waits patiently to expose anyone who only half-remembers it.

s02e11.description: Surveying equipment gets an unlikely moment of television glory with the theodolite. The episode is a celebration of Millionaire’s favourite trick: selecting some specialised object you have definitely seen, then demanding that you know what it is called.
